questions.q: Cesar Concio is most famous for his collaboration on the 'Church of the Holy Sacrifice' at UP Diliman. What is the groundbreaking structural feature of this church?
o: Walls made entirely of stained glass
questions.n: It was the first of its kind in the Philippines, allowing for a massive, column-free interior space.

questions.q: Concio designed the twin 'portal' buildings of UP Diliman that face each other across the University Avenue. What are these two buildings called?
questions.n: These twin buildings (AS and Engineering) serve as the academic anchors of the campus and showcase Concio's clean, functionalist lines.

questions.q: The 'Church of the Holy Sacrifice' is a unique collaboration. Along with Concio, which future National Artist for Architecture worked on the structural design?
questions.n: Locsin was the lead architect; Concio's role was significant in the broader campus context, but Locsin's name is most synonymous with the dome's design.

questions.q: Cesar Concio's style for Palma Hall and Melchor Hall is often described as 'International Style.' What is a key characteristic of this style?
o: Emphasis on volume, lightweight materials, and flat surfaces
Using only local nipa and bamboo
questions.n: This style favored logical, geometric forms and the visible expression of the building's function.

questions.q: Aside from his architectural practice, Cesar Concio held which significant leadership role in architectural education?
o: Chairman of the PRC Board of Architecture
Dean of the UP College of Architecture
Founder of the Mapua Institute of Technology
questions.n: He was a pivotal figure in shaping the architectural curriculum and the physical campus of the University of the Philippines.

questions.q: Cesar Concio’s design for the Church of the Holy Sacrifice features a dome that is only 3 inches thick. How is such a thin structure able to support its own weight and cover a large area?
o: The inherent strength of the shell's curvature and reinforced concrete
Using a special lightweight wood painted to look like concrete
By suspending the roof from external steel cables
The use of massive internal pillars hidden by curtains
questions.n: Thin-shell structures distribute stress through the geometry of the curve rather than through bulk mass.

questions.q: In the design of Palma Hall (AS) and Melchor Hall (Engineering), Concio utilized vertical and horizontal concrete projections to block direct sunlight. What are these called?
questions.n: These functionalist elements were a key part of the International Style's adaptation to the tropical Philippine climate.

questions.q: The Church of the Holy Sacrifice is known for its 'open' feel. How does the base of the dome interact with the surrounding environment?
o: The base is hidden underground to make the dome look like it's floating
The dome rests on 31 pillars with no perimeter walls
It is completely sealed with thick marble walls
It is surrounded by a moat of water to prevent entry
questions.n: By eliminating perimeter walls, Concio allowed for maximum ventilation and a sense of inclusion for those outside.

questions.q: Which specific architectural movement did Concio represent during the post-war reconstruction of the University of the Philippines?
questions.n: Concio and his contemporaries embraced the efficiency and geometric clarity of the Modern movement for the new campus.

questions.q: True or False: Cesar Concio’s design for the Church of the Holy Sacrifice was the first time five future National Artists collaborated on a single project.
questions.n: The project involved Concio, Locsin, Abueva (sculpture), Manansala (murals), and Ang Kiukok (Stations of the Cross).

questions.q: In the twin halls of UP Diliman, what is the significance of the wide, open stairwells and large window banks?
o: To allow for secret meetings between faculty
To increase the cost of the building materials
To provide a place for students to hide from classes
To facilitate natural light and cross-ventilation in large academic buildings
questions.n: Concio designed these spaces to be comfortable for thousands of students without relying solely on electricity.

questions.q: Cesar Concio served as the University Architect of UP. How did his master plan for Diliman differ from the original Burnham plan for Manila?
o: It replaced all trees with paved parking lots
It utilized a decentralized, campus-style layout with wide green spaces
It was designed to be a walled fortress with only one entry
It used a strict radial pattern like a spiderweb
questions.n: Concio's plan focused on the 'Garden Campus' concept, separating academic zones with lush greenery.

questions.q: Which of these materials was the 'star' of Cesar Concio’s mid-century works, allowing him to create both rigid grids and fluid domes?
questions.n: This material defined the era, providing the strength of steel and the versatility of a liquid that could be molded into any shape.

questions.q: The 'Baclaran Church' (National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help) is another massive project Concio worked on. What is its architectural scale relative to other churches in the country?
o: It is one of the largest modern churches, designed to hold thousands of pilgrims
It is a private residence disguised as a church
It was built entirely out of recycled glass bottles
It is the smallest chapel in the Philippines
questions.n: The Modern-Gothic influence allows for a massive interior volume to accommodate the millions who visit each year.

questions.q: What is the primary visual difference between Palma Hall and Melchor Hall, despite them being 'twins'?
o: One has columns and the other has no walls at all
One is painted bright pink and the other is blue
One is a skyscraper and the other is a small bungalow
They are mirror images located on opposite sides of the central academic oval
questions.n: Their symmetry is what defines the 'portal' effect at the entrance of the university's heart.

questions.q: In which major Philippine university can you find the majority of Cesar Concio's most famous institutional buildings?
questions.n: Concio served as the university architect here and designed its twin gateway buildings and the famous chapel.

questions.q: Cesar Concio is associated with the 'Second Generation' of Filipino architects. What was their primary goal after World War II?
o: Embracing Modernism to help in the post-war reconstruction
Rebuilding Manila in the exact style of the Spanish era
Building only wooden structures to save money
Banning the use of concrete in all new buildings
questions.n: Modernism offered a fresh, efficient, and forward-looking aesthetic for a newly independent nation.

questions.q: Which of these is the common name for Palma Hall in UP Diliman, often used by students and faculty?
questions.n: Palma Hall has historically housed the College of Arts and Sciences, hence the nickname 'AS'.

questions.q: True or False: Cesar Concio designed the Protestant 'Church of the Risen Lord' in UP Diliman, which features a distinct parabolic shape.
questions.n: This church is one of his most recognized works, using a parabolic arch to create a unique and modern sacred space.

questions.q: What is the shape of the floor plan of the 'Church of the Holy Sacrifice', which Concio co-designed?
questions.n: The circular plan emphasizes the 'community of believers' gathered around a central altar.

questions.q: In the 'Church of the Risen Lord', what architectural element is used to create the main structural frame?
questions.n: The parabolic arch provides both the structural support and the iconic aesthetic of the chapel.

questions.q: Which of these describe the windows in Concio's Palma Hall?
o: There are no windows, only air conditioning vents
Large glass banks protected by concrete sunshades
Circular portholes like on a ship
Small, narrow slits to keep the building dark
questions.n: This allowed students to have bright classrooms without the intense heat of the tropical sun.

questions.q: True or False: Cesar Concio was known for being one of the first architects to use 'thin-shell' concrete in the Philippines.
questions.n: He was a pioneer in using this advanced engineering technique to create wide-span roofs without many columns.

questions.q: The 'Baclaran Church', which Concio designed, is formally known as what?
o: National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help
questions.n: This is the formal name of the massive church in Baclaran that Concio designed.

questions.q: Cesar Concio's twin buildings at UP (Palma and Melchor) are located at the end of which famous road?
questions.n: The buildings act as a grand entrance or 'portal' at the end of the long University Avenue.
